landmarks.source: Heights, roof shapes and roof colour of the building:part ways are OpenStreetMap (ODbL) and the HRDEM surface model (OGL-Canada). Brick walls with stone dressing, verdigris copper roofs and corner turrets are the look noted in docs/plans/QUEBEC-LOOK.md section 2 (Chateau, gates, churches); that note is the only source for the look. The part of the outline no mapped part covers is filled with parts measured the same way. The round corner turrets (6.0 m across, conical roof 8.5 m, 2.5 m above the eave of the part they stand on) are an estimate: the map has none.

OpenStreetMap: the pedestrian area (surface=wood, layer=1) with the funicular station and four shelters cut out, the viewpoint nodes, 68 mapped benches, cannons with their direction, flagpoles; the balustrade along the cliff edge, the board direction and the lamp spacing are the rule's estimate (board width 0.14 m, boards along the walk, rail 1.1 m, a lamp every 24 m, a planter between them)
OpenStreetMap node (historic=monument, wikidata Q16665231); the tall pedestal with a bronze figure is a simple model, no likeness
